[[File:Venkatesh Narayanamurti in 2023 01.jpg|thumb|Venkatesh Narayanamurti in 2023]]
'''Venkatesh Narayanamurti''' is an American scientist, public policy leader and academic administrator.

He studied physics at [[St. Stephen's College, Delhi]], where he gained his bachelor's degree in 1958 and a master's degree in 1960. He was awarded a PhD by [[Cornell University]] in 1965.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seas.harvard.edu/office-dean/history-office/venkatesh-narayanamurti|title=Venkatesh Narayanamurti|publisher=Harvard University|accessdate=26 July 2020}}</ref>

Narayanamurti is the Benjamin Pierce Research Professor of Technology and Public Policy at [[Harvard University]] where he is a former dean (1998–2008) of the School of Engineering and Applied Sciences.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.hks.harvard.edu/faculty/venkatesh-narayanamurti|title=Venkatesh Narayanamurti|publisher=Harvard Kennedy School|accessdate=2018-04-27}}</ref> Narayanamurti was elected to membership in the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1992 for "developments in the field of phonon optics and leadership in electronic materials and device research and development".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.nae.edu/MembersSection/MemberDirectory/28826.aspx|title=Dr. Venkatesh Narayanamurti|publisher=National Academy of Engineering|accessdate=2018-04-27}}</ref> He also served on the Engineering and Computer Science jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] from 2011 to 2015.{{Citation needed|date=April 2023}}
